newsitem.title: USA: U.S. woman pays $3,500 for scarce "Tickle Me" toy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. woman pays $3,500 for scarce "Tickle Me" toy.

text.p: The hysteria over a fuzzy, red -- and scarce -- toy reached a new level this week when a Florida woman bid $3,500 in a radio auction for a "Tickle Me Elmo" doll.

Denise Flanagan, 44, a retired nurse from Davie, Florida, offered that price, which is 125 times the toy's typical $28 retail tab, in an auction on Tuesday night, although she has no young children or grandchildren.
"My daughter is getting married, and maybe it will go to the first grandchild," Flanagan told the Fort Lauderdale Sun-Sentinel in Wednesday's editions.
Overwhelming demand for the toy this holiday season took New Jersey-based Tyco Toys Inc by surprise and has sent the company scrambling to boost production from 400,000 to 1 million.

Based on a popular character from the "Sesame Street" children's television show, "Tickle Me Elmo" includes a computer chip that makes it giggle and shake and say, "Ooh, that tickles," when its stomach is touched.
The newspaper reported that a woman had recently bid $750 for the doll at a similar charity auction in Boston.
